description: This is a false-colour infrared satellite image displaying a high-altitude mountainous landscape representing alpine and subalpine grasslands. The image is dominated by various shades of red and magenta, indicating vigorous vegetation reflectance typical of healthy plant cover in this spectral composite. Lighter, brownish-green patches suggest areas of sparser vegetation, bare ground, or exposed rock formations, which are characteristic of grasslands mixed with rocks. Scattered small turquoise or cyan features likely represent water bodies or peat bogs, consistent with environments that can have non-permanent water. A distinct green outline delineates a specific area of interest or study boundary within the landscape. A single bright green circular marker (dot) is positioned in the upper-central part of the image, within the outlined region, marking a point of specific interest. The image illustrates land cover patterns typically found above the tree limit in high-mountain regions. The image credit is M. Rodriguez.
